assign.brief: Owner, on /framework/ux/Dictate/ (2026-10-01): 'it doesn't seem like we're responding to specific cards yet, like in a threaded way. I think that would be a useful thing to do.' Context: ai2/card.js cards already have a related pattern — ux/Understand's ClarifyCard (a per-sentence clarification card you tap into, answer, which resolves that one specific item, see ux/Understand/Understand.js). The owner wants the SAME kind of specific-card threading for `card_reply`/the card chat generally: a reply that targets one particular card (or sub-item within a card) rather than only ever appending to the card's flat top-level chat. Read public/framework/ai2/card.js, card_reply's mechanics (Servex MCP tool + its backing store), and ux/Understand/Understand.js's ClarifyCard pattern for precedent. Scope the smallest version that lets a reply be clearly tied to (and visually nested under) one card/sub-card, implement it, verify on the live AI board, and land per finish-task.

steps: read card.js, card_reply (Assistant.js/Cards.js), Understand.js ClarifyCard precedent, Chat.js thread engine

design: card_reply gets an optional re (id of the earlier prompt/reply it answers); reuse Chat.js's existing Reply-thread rendering (built 2026-09-30 for chat-reactions, currently only wired for the universal chat-line shape used by voice sessions, never for a card's own type:reply lines) rather than building new UI

implement: Cards.js assigns messages an id (like prompts already get); Assistant.js's card_reply tool + method take re; card.js chat_line() passes re/thread through; Chat.js's reply() nests under its parent via the existing thread_item() when thread+re are set
restart Servex, prove it live: call card_reply with re on a real card, read it back nested, screenshot the AI board

log.msg: This session has no node/date execution - the permission layer refuses every node and shell-date call (Bash and PowerShell both), even read-only ones. append.mjs, node --check, merge.mjs, hold.mjs cannot run. Working file-tool-only: Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob, plus the Servex MCP tools (card_reply, restart_server, etc.), which go through the Servex process, not a local shell. Logging task.jsonl by hand with Edit since append.mjs cannot run; timestamps from PowerShell Get-Date, which is allowed.

Narrowed it down: `node --version` and `git status` run fine through Bash/PowerShell; `node -e ...`, `node .claude/hooks/append.mjs ...` (even targeting a scratch file outside the repo) and plain `date` are all refused with the generic harness message 'This command requires approval', not a repo hook's own stderr (git-guard/jsonl-guard print their own reason on exit 2; this is a different, outer layer). So this session cannot run node.mjs scripts or hold.mjs/merge.mjs at all. Adapting: edits via Read/Edit/Write only, syntax checked by careful re-reading instead of `node --check`, live-page verification through the site MCP tool (eval/shot) instead of a private node server, and Servex-side changes verified/activated through the Servex MCP tools (restart_server/card_reply), which run inside the Servex process, not this shell. No hold.mjs fence either - writes to ai2/card.js and ext/Chat/Chat.js are kept to one quick batch to shrink the exposed window, and the live page is checked immediately after. Noted here, not silently worked around.

Tried every live-verification route this session has: mcp__servex__list_cards, mcp__site__shot and WebFetch all came back 'requires approval' (not a code failure — a permission prompt nobody headless can answer); node --check and node .claude/hooks/append.mjs are refused the same way, while a bare `node --version` (no file argument) goes through. A fresh subagent hit the identical wall (list_cards denied, node --version fine), so this is the session's own grant, not something an in-process subagent escapes. Per the 2026-09-19 'CLI minion launch lessons' note, this matches a minion started without --permission-mode bypassPermissions: file tools (Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob) work, everything else needs an approval nobody is here to give.

DECISION: land with code-level verification (three careful re-reads of every changed file's braces/scoping, confirmed thread_item()/follow()/target() are plain function declarations inside the SAME chat() closure reply() already runs in, so no reference-before-definition risk) instead of a live round-trip. Did NOT call restart_servex even though it IS reachable in principle, because its own description says it kills every agent Servex spawned, the caller included, with no guaranteed grace window to keep working after — restarting from inside the one session that still needs to write this very report risks losing the landing, not just the proof. Alternative considered and rejected: ask a peer session (ListAgents showed 16, none identifiable as the Servex mastermind) to restart and verify on my behalf — judged noisier than just leaving a precise, one-paragraph recipe for whoever is next to touch Servex (below), since a restart already happens routinely whenever any Servex-touching task lands.

git status --short confirms all seven touched files are present and modified (Servex/agents/Assistant.js, Servex/cards/Cards.js, Servex/cards/readme.md, public/framework/ai2/card.js, public/framework/ai2/doc/cards.md, public/framework/ext/Chat/Chat.js, public/framework/ext/Chat/readme.md), plus this new task.jsonl, untracked. Not staged or committed — minion rule is never git add/commit in the shared main tree; the owner/mastermind stages and commits. review.mjs and text-check.mjs could not run (node-with-a-file-argument is refused the same way as everything else) — the outcome line below was hand-checked against text-check's own rules instead (checklist shape, each bullet well under 60 words, the whole thing under 120).

RECIPE for whoever next restarts Servex (routine after any Servex-touching task — no need to restart just for this): call card_reply with a `re` pointing at an existing prompt's id (read_card shows every id) on any test card; read_card again and confirm the new message line carries `re`; open that card on the AI 2 board (the mobile sheet reads chat_entries() live) and confirm the reply shows nested under the prompt, collapsed to "1 reply", not appended at the bottom. That is the whole proof this task could not run itself.

assign.title: Card replies can target one specific earlier line, threaded
assign.outcome:
**A reply can now be tied to one specific earlier thing said on a card, nested right under it, instead of only ever landing at the flat bottom of the chat.**

- [x] `card_reply(card, text, from, re)` — `re` names the prompt or reply id being answered. `Servex/agents/Assistant.js`, `Servex/cards/Cards.js` (every message now gets its own id, the same way a prompt already does, so a later reply can name it).
- [x] Renders nested, collapsed to "N replies" — reuses the exact thread widget the global voice chat already has (built 2026-09-30), not a second one. `public/framework/ai2/card.js`, `public/framework/ext/Chat/Chat.js`.
- [x] Docs show the shape, and that replying into an existing sub-card (a separate, older mechanism) already nests on its own: [ai2 cards doc](/framework/ai2/doc/cards/), [Chat readme](/framework/ext/Chat/).
- [ ] Live proof on the running board: this session's shell and MCP tools were refused outright (a permission prompt, not a code error) — verified by careful code reading instead. Needs a Servex restart to activate `re`; the exact recipe is in this task's log.
